column1: # Every .env key, for the portal's Settings page and ./stack config (lib/settings.sh). ./stack copies this table into
# .state/status/settings.json together with each value (masked), so the portal never reads .env.
# The update helper takes its allowlist from here (policy column) and checks every value with the validator named
# here (lib/settings.sh: _sv_<validator>; the portal mirrors them in portal/portal/settings.py).
# key  group  secret  policy  validator  apply  label  note  cli
#   group    account | aws | budgets | voice | openrouter | files | updates | remote | advanced (a coarse area, kept in
#            the snapshot; where the Settings page and ./stack config list show a key: catalog/settings-layout.tsv)
#   secret   - plain (shown) | s sensitive, shown (an email, a login) | k key id (first 4 … last 4) | u URL (host only)
#            | h secret, last 4 shown | S secret, nothing shown
#   policy   edit (from the portal; remotely only with REMOTE_ADMIN_ACTIONS=true) | local (only from the computer
#            running bedrock-now) | on-only (may be turned on, never off) | widen-local (the more protective
#            direction anywhere, the other only locally: lib/settings.sh setting_weakens) | companion (only
#            together with its key: PORTAL_PASSWORD_HASH) | regen (only a new random value,
#            made by ./stack: never one the request brings) | ro | derived (written by ./stack)
#   apply    what ./stack config apply does after writing .env (comma list; - = nothing, read when needed); code:
#            ./stack code enable | disable, which write CODE_ENABLED themselves; code-env: the code container is
#            recreated with the new value (while the Code page is on); terminal-env: the terminal container is
#            recreated with it (while the terminal is on: its shells end); remote-preview: the remote preview address
#            again (lib/code.sh code_remote_sync), the sidecar's Services, and the portal and Caddy

column7: Terminal and Code page over remote access
column8: true = the browser terminal is reachable over remote access too (a Tailscale Service of its own). A shell from your phone: turned on in the terminal only.
Written by ./stack while the terminal and REMOTE_TERMINAL are on.
Written by ./stack while the Code page, the terminal and REMOTE_TERMINAL are on.

Off by default. true = the Code page's previews of dev servers in the sandbox work over remote access too (wherever the Code page does: REMOTE_TERMINAL=true), at one more address: svc:<name>-preview with Tailscale, or preview.<your domain>. The trade-off: a page your sandbox serves then becomes same-site with every other app on your tailnet (all of <tailnet>.ts.net) or your whole domain — its script could send those apps requests carrying their cookies, and set or flood cookies for the whole site. bedrock-now's own hosts refuse such requests (the same-site guard); your other apps may not. With Tailscale, define and approve the Service <name>-preview in the admin console first. In own-domain mode REMOTE_PREVIEW_DOMAIN (a domain of their own) avoids the trade-off, and blank means on there. Turning it on works only from the computer running bedrock-now; off works everywhere. The portal and Caddy restart (about 10 s).

Own-domain mode: a name on a registrable domain of its own for the previews (blank = preview.<your domain>, the portal's site), so they are another site than the portal's and your domain's other apps — and previews over remote access are then on unless REMOTE_PREVIEW=false. Needs its DNS record, and the Cloudflare token for its zone too.

true = the Terminal tab: Claude Code in a sandbox container that sees one folder of yours. On by default with the Code page (blank: setup and updates turn both on; false keeps them off). Turned on and off in the terminal: it builds an image, checks the folder and asks LiteLLM for a key.
The workspace: the folder of this computer the terminal sees at /workspace (besides any Project folders), checked against the folders it must never see.

internet (the default; blank is the same): the sandbox of the Terminal and the Code page reaches public internet addresses (npm, pip, git, documentation, Claude Code's web fetch) through its egress proxy, on ports 80, 443 and 22 — never this computer's own services, your local network, private or link-local addresses: the proxy refuses them after its own DNS lookup, and nothing in the sandbox has another route (TERMINAL_EGRESS_ALLOW and TERMINAL_EGRESS_DENY narrow it further). host: the sandbox itself on the internet, with this computer's own services (on Docker Desktop: LiteLLM, the shared MCP server, the portal's login and dev servers on its 127.0.0.1, through Docker's host address) and your local network — any address, any port, as v0.10.0 and earlier always did. off: no internet; only LiteLLM and the shared MCP server through its gateway. The old on value (true/1/yes/on) reads as internet. Opening it further (off, internet, host) works only from the computer running bedrock-now; closing it works everywhere. The terminal restarts (about 10 s; its shells and open Code sessions end), and the Code page with it.
column9: ./stack config set TERMINAL_EGRESS (then: internet, host or off)

column8: Blank (the default) = every public name. Otherwise a comma list of the names the sandbox's egress proxy lets it reach — each with the names under it (github.com covers api.github.com) — and nothing else. name:PORT (or *:PORT) opens that port instead of 80, 443 and 22; * stands for every name (*,git.example.com:8443 = every name as before, plus that port there). Never an IP address: private ones stay refused whatever this says. Only with TERMINAL_EGRESS=internet; refusals are in ./stack logs terminal-egress.

A comma list of names the sandbox's egress proxy refuses — each with the names under it; name:PORT for that port only — whatever TERMINAL_EGRESS_ALLOW says. While it is set, IP addresses are refused too (a denied site's address would not match its name): only names go out. Blank (the default) = none. Only with TERMINAL_EGRESS=internet.
Blank = terminal.PORTAL_HOST.
The terminal container's memory limit (blank = 4g).
Yours, so files in the workspace stay yours (10104 when ./stack runs as root).
Yours, like the user id.
The header the main Caddy adds and the terminal's gateway requires before ttyd. Internal: never shown; a new one at every enable.

true = the Code tab: Claude Code in the browser with a chat, permission prompts and your workspace's files, in the browser terminal's sandbox (the same folder, key and budget). It reaches public internet addresses, through the sandbox's egress proxy — not this computer's own services or your network (TERMINAL_EGRESS: Sandbox internet access). On by default: blank means setup and updates turn it on (with the terminal and its default folder); false keeps it off. Turning it on builds an image (a few minutes) and turns the browser terminal on too when it is off (with its folder: TERMINAL_WORKSPACE, or the default one): only from the computer running bedrock-now. Turning it off works from anywhere; the terminal stays.

true = the Code page's mode picker also offers Bypass permissions: Claude runs every command and edit in the sandbox without asking, in one session at a time and only after a confirmation that names the risks (never remembered: a resumed or restarted session goes on in Manual, a new one in your usual mode). Deny rules still deny; Claude's file tools still ask before changing .git, .claude, .vscode, .husky, .devcontainer, .envrc or .mcp.json, shell commands do not — files that run on your computer are flagged after each turn, with Revert. It works on your real workspace folder, with the sandbox's internet access (TERMINAL_EGRESS), also over remote access once allowed here. Turning it on works only from the computer running bedrock-now; off works everywhere. The code container restarts (about 10 s; open Code sessions end, a prompt resumes them).

true = the Code page's mode picker also offers Auto (Claude Code's auto mode): a reviewer model checks each shell command, web fetch and other action that would otherwise ask you, lets the routine ones run and blocks the risky ones (downloading and running code, sending data out, force pushes …) with the rule it matched. File edits in the workspace and read-only commands run without it; your ask rules still ask; Plan still asks you; a blocked action can be allowed once from its card. The reviewer runs on Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Claude Code asks for claude-sonnet-5, which the catalog maps to it; without Sonnet 5.5 on your key it uses the session's own model), on the terminal's key and budget: measured about $0.13 for the first check in each 5 minutes (it sends ~47k tokens of instructions, cached) and about half a cent for each further check — more than a Haiku session itself costs. A model judging actions can be wrong either way: the sandbox stays the boundary. Turning it on works only from the computer running bedrock-now; off works everywhere. The code container restarts, and the browser terminal too unless its own Auto mode is on (about 10 s; open Code sessions end — a prompt resumes them — and so do the terminal's shells).

The GitHub App that Git hosts' Sign in with GitHub signs in with: its client ID (Iv…), a public value — no client secret or private key is ever needed (the device flow). Blank = bedrock-now's own app (github.com/apps/bedrock-now); for an app of your own (README › Remote repositories: Your own app for sign-in), put its client ID here. The app reaches only the repositories it is installed on, with its permissions. Only from the computer running bedrock-now: another app is another party you would authorize. The code container restarts (about 10 s; open Code sessions end, a prompt resumes them).

That app's name as its address has it (github.com/apps/NAME), for Git hosts' Choose repositories link (where you install it on your repositories). Blank = bedrock-now's own app's name; with your own client ID, put your app's name here too. The code container restarts (about 10 s).

The gitlab.com application that Git hosts' Sign in with GitLab signs in with: its application ID, a public value (a non-confidential application: no secret). Blank = none: gitlab.com has no bedrock-now application, so Sign in with GitLab there needs one of your own (README › Remote repositories: Your own app for sign-in) — put its application ID here. A GitLab of your own takes its application ID in the Git hosts dialog instead. Only from the computer running bedrock-now. The code container restarts (about 10 s; open Code sessions end, a prompt resumes them).

true = Claude Code's auto mode in the browser terminal too (claude and claude-bedrock there): the same reviewer model on Claude Sonnet 5.5 approves routine actions and blocks risky ones instead of asking you, at the same cost (about $0.13 per 5 minutes in use plus about half a cent per check, on the terminal's key). As anywhere else, an interactive claude then starts in it unless ~/.claude/settings.json there sets another permissions.defaultMode; Shift+Tab leaves it. Off (the default): auto mode is off for every claude in the sandbox — with the Code page's Auto mode on, claude typed in its shells and claude-bedrock still keep it off (a convenience: /usr/local/bin/claude called directly does not). Turning it on works only from the computer running bedrock-now; off works everywhere. The terminal restarts (about 10 s; its shells and open Code sessions end).
Blank = code.PORTAL_HOST.
The header the main Caddy adds and the code container requires. Internal: never shown; a new one at every enable.

The Code page's previews of dev servers in the sandbox are at p<port>-<capability>.PREVIEW_DOMAIN, derived from PORTAL_HOST (bedrock-now-preview.localhost): another site than the portal's, so none of its cookies reach them. Local only for now.
The header the main Caddy adds to a preview's requests and the terminal's gateway requires before bn-preview. Internal: never shown; a new one at every enable.
